---
title: "Size: Placebo Adoption Years Under the Inference Rule"
format: html
execute:
  echo: true
  message: false
  warning: false
---

The inference rule clusters standard errors by unit. This exploration checks that a test at the
10% level rejects about 10% of the time when there is no effect. Each placebo permutation draws
a fake adoption year and gives it to a random half of the never-treated units, so the true
effect is zero by construction; the main specification is then estimated on the never-treated
units alone. The rejection rate is copied into the manuscript's `design.checks.size`.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)

set.seed(20260908L)

# Placebo permutations. Small, so the fixture renders quickly; the Monte Carlo error of the
# rejection rate is reported below.
N_PERMUTATIONS <- 200L
TEST_LEVEL <- 0.10
```

```{r}
#| label: placebo-permutations
panel <- read_csv(here("data/raw/panel.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# Never-treated units carry no effect, so any placebo "effect" among them is noise.
never_treated <- panel |>
  group_by(unit) |>
  filter(max(treated) == 0) |>
  ungroup()
control_units <- sort(unique(never_treated$unit))
stopifnot("never-treated units exist" = length(control_units) > 1)

# Placebo adoption years leave at least two pre-period and two post-period years.
placebo_years <- seq(min(panel$year) + 2L, max(panel$year) - 1L)

placebo_p_value <- function(permutation_id) {
  placebo_units <- sample(control_units, length(control_units) %/% 2)
  placebo_year <- sample(placebo_years, 1)
  panel_placebo <- never_treated |>
    mutate(placebo_treated = as.integer(unit %in% placebo_units & year >= placebo_year))
  fit_placebo <- feols(outcome ~ placebo_treated | unit + year, data = panel_placebo, cluster = ~unit)
  tibble(permutation = permutation_id, placebo_year = placebo_year,
         p_value = pvalue(fit_placebo)[["placebo_treated"]])
}
placebo_results <- map(seq_len(N_PERMUTATIONS), placebo_p_value) |> list_rbind()
```

```{r}
#| label: rejection-rate
rejection_rate <- mean(placebo_results$p_value <= TEST_LEVEL)
rejection_mc_se <- sqrt(TEST_LEVEL * (1 - TEST_LEVEL) / N_PERMUTATIONS)
```

## Result

Across `r N_PERMUTATIONS` placebo permutations the clustered test rejects at the
`r round(100 * TEST_LEVEL)`% level in **`r round(rejection_rate, 3)`** of them (Monte Carlo SE
`r round(rejection_mc_se, 3)` around a nominal `r TEST_LEVEL`).

Recorded in the manuscript's `design.checks.size`: rejection_at_0.10 `r round(rejection_rate, 3)`,
reps `r N_PERMUTATIONS`.
